label: Malted milk
step: mix with malt extract and flour, dry
note: Invented as an infant food: James Horlick, a London pharmacist, formed J & W Horlicks in 1873, patent 1883 for a formula with dried milk; the name malted milk was trademarked 1887.

about.text: A powder of malted barley, wheat flour and dried whole milk, stirred into hot or cold milk or water. It began as an infant food and became a drink and a flavour of sweets.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.

how.text: Wheat flour and ground barley malt are mashed, so the malt enzymes convert insoluble starch into sugars (maltose, dextrins). The mash extract is mixed with milk, evaporated to a syrup in a vacuum pan and dried under vacuum to a powder. Whether the milk goes in fresh or as powder varies; the arrow in the graph starts from milk powder, the modern route. No source I could open gave mash temperature, time or the malt/flour/milk ratio.

steps.name: mash
steps.note: Wheat flour and ground barley malt are mashed, the malt amylases turning starch into maltose and dextrins.
The mash extract is mixed with milk or milk powder.
Concentrated in a vacuum pan to a heavy syrup.
Dried under vacuum on shelves, to about 3 % moisture or less.
